validation_scope: Project-authored review against the pinned RFC excerpts; not independent human or domain-expert validation.

retrieval_miss_findings.finding: Neither variant retrieved the RFC 9110 definition chunk. Both refusals were faithful to their unrelated excerpts, but the end-to-end answer was incomplete.
Neither variant retrieved the exact complex-request prose. Both saw adjacent HTTP/2 framing chunks, then incorrectly put END_STREAM on HEADERS and omitted the required DATA-frame sequence.

Both variants retrieved the RFC 9931 mitigation but missed the RFC 9112 authority-form chunk. They instead retrieved an absolute-form chunk that explicitly excludes CONNECT and gave the wrong request-target while answering the mitigation half correctly.

Body retrieval found related QPACK capacity text but neither exact gold chunk. Metadata retrieval found the exact capacity-instruction chunk at rank four but not the HTTP/3 rationale chunk. Both conservatively refused rather than answer only half.

cases.finding: Both answers state the exact zero-length byte-range rule. Body adds a true but non-discriminating general note that servers may ignore Range.

Both cover gateways, accelerator caching, and load balancing, while both omit the legacy/untrusted-service use. Metadata adds response-time and backend-load claims not stated in its retrieved excerpts; body stays within the evidence.

Both correctly explain trailer sections. Metadata adds an accurate Trailer-field detail visible in a retrieved example. The judge rationale overstates this as a mandatory declaration, which neither the answer nor gold evidence claims.
Answers are semantically identical and fully supported. Adding the word HTTP before upgrade tokens does not create a material quality difference in this question.
Both contain the required h2, h3, preface, and SETTINGS facts. Metadata is clearer; body first says both sides send a connection preface before correctly distinguishing HTTP/3 SETTINGS.

unanswerable_review.finding: Neither retrieved bundle states a worker-thread-per-CPU-core default.
Retrieved caching excerpts define shared/private caches and storage rules but no disk-space-per-user reservation.

correctness_summary.note: Manual findings agree with the absolute judge on the substantive q007 and q016 errors. Pairwise disagreements above show why raw 4-1-16 blind counts should not be presented without review.
